question: Can air defences keep up with drones, yes or no?

lines.text: Six hundred and thirteen drones flew at Moscow overnight, the city's mayor says.
Russia's defence ministry says it downed one thousand two hundred and fourteen nationwide.
Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says two hundred and thirty one were destroyed approaching Moscow.
He says most were neutralised by the defence ministry's air defence forces on the distant approaches.

scene.quote: Most were neutralised by the defence ministry's air defence forces on the distant approaches

lines.text: Flights were restricted at three Moscow airports: Vnukovo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky.
Russia's aviation agency says the limits were lifted by morning.
The ministry lists sixteen regions, plus Moscow region, Bashkortostan and Udmurtia.
In Bashkortostan, Ufa airport halted all flights, and residents of Sterlitamak reported explosions.
Russian outlet Astra says smoke rose over the Bashkir Soda Company plant there.
Ukrainian media say the plant makes materials used in body armour.
Kyiv has not commented. Its air force says Russia sent one hundred and twelve drones at Ukraine.
Sobyanin says the biggest wave came in mid September, about sixteen hundred drones in a day.
Over twelve hundred in one night. Can air defences keep up with drones, yes or no?
